object: British philosopher, logician, and mathematician (1872–1970).  Nobel Prize in Literature 1950. Co-authored /Principia Mathematica/ with Whitehead — the most ambitious attempt to ground mathematics in pure logic.  Russell's paradox had exposed the cracks; /Principia/ was the repair job; Gödel showed the cracks were structural.
